description: Process flowcharts: steps, decisions, inputs and outputs joined by flow edges. Read this before writing a flowchart so kinds are valid first time; unknown kinds are accepted but flagged by lint.

nodeKinds.name: terminal
nodeKinds.description: Start or end of the process.

nodeKinds.name: process
nodeKinds.description: A step or action.

nodeKinds.name: decision
nodeKinds.description: A branch; outgoing flow edges carry the condition as their label.

nodeKinds.name: io
nodeKinds.description: Input or output: a form, file, message or report.

nodeKinds.name: subprocess
nodeKinds.description: A step defined in another document.

props.documentId: Id of the document that defines the subprocess

nodeKinds.name: note
nodeKinds.description: Annotation attached to nothing in particular.

nodeKinds.name: container
nodeKinds.description: A swimlane or grouping; children reference it via parent.

nodeKinds.name: pool
nodeKinds.description: A swimlane pool: a container with a title band that holds lanes and the process steps inside them.

props.orientation: horizontal (lanes are rows, top to bottom) or vertical (lanes are columns, left to right)

nodeKinds.name: lane
nodeKinds.description: A lane inside a swimlane pool: a band holding the steps that belong to one participant or team.

nodeKinds.name: text
nodeKinds.description: Free-standing text with no box.

nodeKinds.name: image
nodeKinds.description: An uploaded image; props.assetId points at the asset.

props.assetId: Asset id of the uploaded image

nodeKinds.name: sticky
nodeKinds.description: A coloured note for review comments; not part of the process.

nodeKinds.name: delay
nodeKinds.description: A waiting period before the flow continues.

nodeKinds.name: manual-operation
nodeKinds.description: An operation or adjustment made by hand rather than by the system.

nodeKinds.name: display
nodeKinds.description: Information shown to a person on a screen or display.

nodeKinds.name: stored-data
nodeKinds.description: Data held in a store for later use, such as a file or record.

nodeKinds.name: merge
nodeKinds.description: Several flows combine into a single flow.

nodeKinds.name: extract
nodeKinds.description: One flow splits into several flows.

nodeKinds.name: loop-limit
nodeKinds.description: The start or end of a loop; the loop-back edge attaches here.

nodeKinds.name: initial
nodeKinds.description: The start pseudostate: a filled circle where a state machine begins.

nodeKinds.name: final
nodeKinds.description: The final state: a ringed dot where a state machine stops.

nodeKinds.name: choice
nodeKinds.description: A choice pseudostate: one incoming transition and several guarded outgoing branches.

nodeKinds.name: fork-join
nodeKinds.description: A fork or join bar: one transition splits into several, or several merge into one.

nodeKinds.name: shallow-history
nodeKinds.description: A shallow-history pseudostate: resume at the last active direct substate.

nodeKinds.name: deep-history
nodeKinds.description: A deep-history pseudostate: resume at the last active state however deeply nested.

nodeKinds.name: entry-point
nodeKinds.description: An entry point: where a transition enters a composite state.

nodeKinds.name: exit-point
nodeKinds.description: An exit point: where a transition leaves a composite state.

nodeKinds.name: composite-state
nodeKinds.description: A composite state: a state that contains its own nested states and transitions; children reference it via parent.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-start
nodeKinds.description: BPMN none start event: a thin-ringed circle where a process begins with no defined trigger. Give it one outgoing flow edge and no incoming one.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-start-message
nodeKinds.description: BPMN message start event: the process begins when a message arrives. Draw a message-flow edge into it from the sending pool or participant.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-start-timer
nodeKinds.description: BPMN timer start event: the process begins at a set time or on a schedule.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-start-signal
nodeKinds.description: BPMN signal start event: the process begins when a broadcast signal is received.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-intermediate
nodeKinds.description: BPMN none intermediate event: a double-ringed circle marking a milestone or state change part-way through a process, with one incoming and one outgoing flow edge.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-intermediate-message
nodeKinds.description: BPMN message catch event: the flow waits at this point until a message arrives; draw a message-flow edge into it.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-intermediate-message-throw
nodeKinds.description: BPMN message throw event (filled envelope): the flow sends a message here and carries on; draw a message-flow edge out of it to the receiver.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-intermediate-timer
nodeKinds.description: BPMN timer intermediate event: the flow waits at this point for a duration or until a date.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-intermediate-error
nodeKinds.description: BPMN error boundary event: place it on the edge of an activity to catch an error that activity raises; its outgoing flow is the error path. It has no incoming flow.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-intermediate-signal
nodeKinds.description: BPMN signal catch event: the flow waits at this point until a broadcast signal is received.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-intermediate-signal-throw
nodeKinds.description: BPMN signal throw event (filled triangle): the flow broadcasts a signal here and carries on.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-intermediate-link
nodeKinds.description: BPMN link catch event: the target of a jump from a link throw event with the same label, used to continue a flow without a long connector.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-intermediate-link-throw
nodeKinds.description: BPMN link throw event (filled arrow): jumps to the link catch event with the same label; it has no outgoing flow.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-end
nodeKinds.description: BPMN none end event: a thick-ringed circle where one path of the process ends. It has incoming flow and no outgoing flow.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-end-message
nodeKinds.description: BPMN message end event: the path ends by sending a message; draw a message-flow edge out of it to the receiver.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-end-error
nodeKinds.description: BPMN error end event: the path ends by raising an error, which an error boundary event on an enclosing activity catches.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-end-signal
nodeKinds.description: BPMN signal end event: the path ends by broadcasting a signal.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-task
nodeKinds.description: BPMN task: one unit of work of no particular type, a rounded rectangle with one incoming and one outgoing flow edge.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-user-task
nodeKinds.description: BPMN user task: work a person does with the help of a software application.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-service-task
nodeKinds.description: BPMN service task: work done automatically by a service or system, with no person involved.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-script-task
nodeKinds.description: BPMN script task: work done by the process engine running a script.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-manual-task
nodeKinds.description: BPMN manual task: work a person does with no software support.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-send-task
nodeKinds.description: BPMN send task: work whose job is to send a message to another participant; draw a message-flow edge out of it.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-receive-task
nodeKinds.description: BPMN receive task: work that waits for a message from another participant; draw a message-flow edge into it.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-business-rule-task
nodeKinds.description: BPMN business rule task: work that evaluates a decision table or rules engine.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-sub-process
nodeKinds.description: BPMN collapsed sub-process: a step whose detail is drawn elsewhere, shown with a plus marker. For an expanded sub-process use a container and parent its steps to it.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-call-activity
nodeKinds.description: BPMN call activity: a thick-bordered step that invokes a reusable process or global task defined elsewhere.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-exclusive-gateway
nodeKinds.description: BPMN exclusive gateway (X): exactly one outgoing path is taken, so label every outgoing flow with its condition. As a merge it passes on whichever single path arrives.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-parallel-gateway
nodeKinds.description: BPMN parallel gateway (+): splits the flow into all outgoing paths at once, or waits for every incoming path before continuing; its flows carry no conditions.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-inclusive-gateway
nodeKinds.description: BPMN inclusive gateway (O): one or more outgoing paths are taken, each whose condition is true; as a merge it waits for every path that was taken.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-event-gateway
nodeKinds.description: BPMN event-based gateway: the path taken is decided by which following event happens first, so each outgoing flow leads to a catch event or receive task.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-complex-gateway
nodeKinds.description: BPMN complex gateway (asterisk): routing by a rule too involved for the other gateways; state the rule in its label.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-data-object
nodeKinds.description: BPMN data object: a document or piece of data an activity uses or produces; link it to the activity with a data-association edge.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-data-store
nodeKinds.description: BPMN data store: a database or repository that outlives the process, which activities read from or write to through data-association edges.

nodeKinds.name: bpmn-annotation
nodeKinds.description: BPMN text annotation: a comment on the diagram, attached to the element it explains with a bpmn-association edge. It is not part of the flow.

edgeKinds.name: flow
edgeKinds.description: Control passes from one step to the next. Label decision branches (Yes / No). In a BPMN diagram this is the sequence flow between events, activities and gateways inside one pool.

edgeKinds.name: association
edgeKinds.description: A non-directional link, typically note to step.

edgeKinds.name: message-flow
edgeKinds.description: A BPMN message flow: a message sent between two different pools or participants, drawn dashed with an open circle at the tail. Never use it between two nodes of the same pool.

edgeKinds.name: bpmn-association
edgeKinds.description: A BPMN association: a dotted, non-directional link from a text annotation to the element it comments on.

edgeKinds.name: data-association
edgeKinds.description: A BPMN data association: a dotted arrow from a data object or store to the activity that reads it, or from an activity to the data object or store it writes.
